classification.difficultyReason: Requires reversing a percentage decrease and recognising that the restoring increase uses the reduced population as its base.

content.prompt: The population of a town decreases by 11% during 2012. What percentage increase is necessary during 2013 for the population to be restored to its population immediately before 2012? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$12.36\%$ increase.

Express the original population as a percentage of the reduced population, then subtract $100\%$.
answer.worked:
Take the population immediately before 2012 as $100$ units.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Population after 2012}&=100(1-0.11)\\\text{Population after 2012}&=89\end{align*}$$

Using the reduced population as the base:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Required percentage increase}&=\left(\frac{100}{89}\times100-100\right)\%\\\text{Required percentage increase}&=\frac{1100}{89}\%\\\text{Required percentage increase}&\approx12.36\%\end{align*}$$
